def fruit_distribution(s, n):
    lis = list()
    for i in s.split(' '):
        if i.isdigit():
            lis.append(int(i))
    return n - sum(lis)

# Unit test for function fruit_distribution
def test_fruit_distribution():
    # Basic cases with known quantities
    assert fruit_distribution("5 apples and 6 oranges", 19) == 8
    assert fruit_distribution("5 apples and 6 oranges", 11) == 0
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 1 oranges", 3) == 2
    assert fruit_distribution("1 apples and 1 oranges", 10) == 8
    assert fruit_distribution("2 apples and 3 oranges", 100) == 95
    assert fruit_distribution("100 apples and 1 oranges", 120) == 19
    
    # Zero counts of named fruits
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 0 oranges", 3) == 3
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 0 oranges", 0) == 0
    
    # Multi-digit numbers
    assert fruit_distribution("12 apples and 34 oranges", 100) == 54
    assert fruit_distribution("999 apples and 999 oranges", 2000) == 2
    
    # String with no digits
    assert fruit_distribution("apples and oranges", 10) == 10
    assert fruit_distribution("", 5) == 5
    
    # Numbers embedded in larger words are not counted (isdigit fails)
    assert fruit_distribution("apples5 and oranges", 10) == 10
    
    # Single fruit type mentioned
    assert fruit_distribution("7 mangoes", 10) == 3
    
    print("All tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_fruit_distribution()
